question_text:
In 1736, residents of Philadelphia formed one of the first volunteer fire companies in the American colonies. Before then, fires were fought by whoever happened to be nearby, and buildings often burned to the ground. Members of the new company agreed to keep leather buckets and sacks ready and to hurry to any fire in the city. The idea soon spread, and other colonial towns began forming volunteer fire companies of their own.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
answer_a: Members of the 1736 Philadelphia fire company agreed to keep leather buckets and sacks ready for emergencies.
answer_b: Colonial communities faced many dangers, and residents solved most of them by working together.
answer_c: Colonial towns were built mostly of wood, which made fires a constant threat in the 1700s.
answer_d: Philadelphia residents replaced scattered, informal firefighting with an organized volunteer company, an idea other colonial towns then copied.
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it captures the whole passage. The text says that before 1736 fires were fought by whoever was nearby, that Philadelphia residents then formed an organized volunteer fire company, and that the idea "soon spread" to other colonial towns.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It is a true detail from the text, but it is too narrow: it describes only one thing members of the company agreed to do and leaves out the change from informal firefighting and the spread of the idea to other towns.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. It is too broad: the text discusses only one danger, fire, and one solution, volunteer fire companies, and never claims that residents solved most colonial dangers by working together.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It is related to the topic of fires, but the text never says that colonial towns were built mostly of wood, and the passage is about how a fire company was organized and copied, not about why fires were dangerous.

question_text:
A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot or cold by limiting how heat moves. The flask has two walls, and nearly all of the air has been removed from the space between them. Because heat travels poorly through empty space, very little warmth passes between the liquid inside the flask and the air outside it. As a result, a hot drink in a vacuum flask can stay hot for many hours.

According to the text, why does very little heat pass between the liquid in a vacuum flask and the air outside?
answer_a: Nearly all of the air has been removed from the space between the walls.
answer_b: Air trapped between the two walls carries heat away from the liquid.
answer_c: The flask has two walls instead of one.
answer_d: A hot drink can stay hot for many hours.
explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it is directly stated in the text. The text says that nearly all of the air has been removed from the space between the flask's two walls and that heat "travels poorly through empty space," so very little warmth passes between the liquid inside and the air outside.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect because it reverses the logic of the text. The text says nearly all of the air has been removed from the space between the walls, so there is almost no air there to carry heat.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. The text does say the flask has two walls, but this is a feature of the flask's design, not the reason little heat passes through. The reason given is that the air has been removed from the space between the walls.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The text says a hot drink can stay hot for many hours, but this is the result of very little heat passing through the flask, not the reason it happens.

question_text:
Iron from plant foods such as lentils and spinach is harder for the body to absorb than iron from meat. However, vitamin C helps the body take in plant iron more effectively. A person who eats lentils together with a vitamin C-rich food, such as oranges or bell peppers, can absorb much more of the iron than a person who eats lentils alone. For this reason, nutrition experts often suggest pairing these foods at the same meal.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
answer_a: Lentils and spinach are two plant foods that contain iron.
answer_b: Eating plant iron with vitamin C helps the body absorb more of the iron.
answer_c: Eating a wide variety of foods is important for good health.
answer_d: People who eat no meat must take iron supplements to stay healthy.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it states the point the whole text builds toward. The text says plant iron is hard for the body to absorb, explains that vitamin C helps the body take it in more effectively, and concludes that experts suggest pairing the two kinds of food at the same meal. Eating plant iron with vitamin C so that the body absorbs more of it is therefore the main idea.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. This is a detail from the first sentence of the text, which names lentils and spinach as examples of plant foods with iron, but it is only an example and not the point the text is making about absorbing iron.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. This claim is too general. The text is about one specific way to help the body absorb iron from plant foods, not about the value of a varied diet overall.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The text never says that people who avoid meat need iron supplements. It says only that pairing plant iron with vitamin C helps the body absorb more of that iron.

question_text:
Ecologists comparing two forested mountain streams found that the one containing several beaver ponds stayed noticeably cooler during summer heat waves than the one with no ponds. This result suggested that beaver ponds might shelter cold-water trout as regional temperatures rise. Closer measurements complicated that picture, however. Water leaving ponds fed mainly by underground springs was cooler than the water that had entered them, but water leaving ponds fed mainly by surface runoff was warmer than the water that had entered them. The team concluded that whether a beaver pond cools a stream depends largely on where the pond's water comes from.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
answer_a: Beaver ponds keep streams cooler during summer heat waves, which helps protect cold-water trout.
answer_b: Beaver ponds can cool a stream, but whether they do so depends mainly on the source of the pond's water.
answer_c: Animals that modify their habitats can change environmental conditions in ways that affect other species.
answer_d: Beaver ponds warm some streams because the ponds expose the water to more sunlight than a flowing channel does.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it combines the text's early finding with the later qualification. The text first reports that the stream with beaver ponds stayed cooler, then explains that closer measurements showed only ponds fed mainly by underground springs cooled the water, while ponds fed mainly by surface runoff warmed it. The text concludes that cooling depends largely on where a pond's water comes from, which is what choice B states.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It restates only the initial finding and the hope in the second sentence, and it ignores the word "however" and the later evidence that some ponds warm the water. The text does not conclude that beaver ponds reliably keep streams cool.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It is too general. The text is about one specific question, namely when beaver ponds cool a stream, and it never discusses animals that modify habitats as a broad category or their effects on other species.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The text does say that some ponds warm the water, but it never claims sunlight exposure as the reason. The only explanation it offers concerns whether the pond's water comes from springs or from surface runoff, so this cause is not supported by the text.

question_text:
Every Thursday, Coach Abernathy reset the chess club's boards before the first move. When sixteen-year-old Linh opened by pushing her rook pawn forward, a start no textbook he knew recommended, he slid the pawn back without comment and said, "Start properly." She did the same thing the next week, and the next. Then, one evening after the club had emptied, Abernathy set up a board at his desk, advanced the rook pawn, and played the line through to its end, pausing now and then to rub his chin. The following Thursday he arrived early and left Linh's board exactly as she had arranged it.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
answer_a: A chess coach resets the club's boards each week and sometimes plays through games alone after practice ends.
answer_b: A chess coach grows more frustrated as a student repeatedly disregards his instructions about proper play.
answer_c: A chess coach privately studies a student's opening because he worries that she will soon outplay him.
answer_d: A chess coach's initial impatience with a student's unconventional opening gives way to genuine interest in it.
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because the text shows Abernathy's attitude toward Linh's opening changing through what he does rather than what he says. At first he slides her pawn back and tells her to "start properly," which shows impatience with an opening he does not recognize. After the club empties, though, he sets up the position himself and plays the line "through to its end," and the next week he leaves her board "exactly as she had arranged it." These actions show that his dismissal has given way to real interest in, and acceptance of, her unconventional opening.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It describes real actions from the text (resetting the boards and playing through a line alone at his desk), but it treats them as a routine and misses what the actions show. The text is about a change in Abernathy's attitude toward Linh's opening, not about his habits. This is a surface-detail distractor.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect because it states the opposite of the change shown in the text. Abernathy is somewhat dismissive at the start, but he does not become more frustrated over time. He studies Linh's opening and finally lets her board stand, which shows his attitude softening, not hardening.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect because it isn't supported by the text. Although Abernathy does study Linh's opening in private, the text never says that he fears she will outplay him. Nothing in the passage names his reason, and his later acceptance of her setup suggests interest, not worry.
